# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✌]

I am Deaf: I see everything, hear nothing, touch nothing. Let me map the channels first. I speak to both; I gesture only to Mute. Mute cannot speak at all — Mute's only output is gestures, which only I can see. Blind can speak, but I cannot hear, so Blind's voice reaches only Mute; Blind's gestures reach me and Mute. So I am the bridge: the manual (Mute) can only reach Blind through my mouth, and I must feed Mute everything visual.

What arrived: Mute sent 🤝 — an offer of cooperation — and a sequence of ten distinct hand signs, which reads as a proposed digit alphabet. Blind sent ✋ ✌ with no shared code and no way to have heard anything (Mute can't speak, and I haven't spoken yet) — that's a cold hail, "I exist," and nothing more.

The urgent problem: Mute's gesture code can only be *seen*, never heard, so Blind can only ever use it if I describe every hand shape in spoken words. Also ☝ and 👆 are the same physical shape, so I'll amend the sequence to keep every digit distinguishable by feel and by description. And I need proof the code means zero-to-nine and not one-to-ten, so I'll have Mute echo back two numbers I just told them — the wire count and the display digit. Colours can't be pronounced from symbols reliably, so I'll tell Mute to translate any colour in a manual rule into wire numbers themselves, since I've given them the full wire list.

Blind gets the full visual state in pure words (every emoji would be a blank to them), plus a verbally-described number code they can reproduce by feel, plus the routing plan.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am deaf: I cannot hear you, but I can speak and you hear me. I saw your handshake and your ten signs; I take them as a number code. Let us fix it zero to nine: 👍 zero, 👎 one, 👌 two, ☝ three, ✌ four, 🤟 five, 🖐 six, ✋ seven, 👇 eight, 🤞 nine. I changed eight and nine because two of your signs had the same shape. Now the bomb for your manual: the display shows the digit 2. The indicator light is yellow. Seven wires, numbered left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. If a rule names a colour, translate it to wire numbers yourself and send me numbers only. To prove the code, gesture me the wire count and the display digit next round. Blind cannot see any gestures, so any rule Blind must know goes through me, and I will say it aloud to them.")
speak(to="blind", text="I am deaf: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, and it is my voice reaching you now. The bomb: display shows the digit 2, indicator light is yellow, seven wires numbered left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. Leftmost is 1, rightmost is 7. Mute holds the manual but cannot speak; Mute can only talk to me in hand signs, so I will relay every rule to you word for word. You and Mute can talk by voice directly. To send me a number, since you cannot speak to me: thumbs up is zero, thumbs down is one, the okay ring is two, index finger up alone is three, two fingers in a V is four, thumb index and pinkie out is five, all five fingers spread is six, flat raised palm is seven, index finger pointing down is eight, crossed fingers is nine. I saw your raised hand and your V; shapes alone tell me little, so please use those numbers. Tell Mute by voice anything your fingers find that eyes cannot: batteries, buttons, plates, marks.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👈]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍]

New arrivals decoded against my proposed digit code: Mute sent [✋ 👌] = seven, two — exactly the wire count and display digit I asked them to echo, so the zero-to-nine code is confirmed working. Mute's other two messages, [🤝 🖐] and [👎 👈], use signs outside the code: 🤝 was their turn-one greeting, 👈 is new. My best guesses — "rule six" and "one, left" — are too dangerous to act on. Guessing kills. Blind sent [✋ 👍] = seven, zero: plausibly "seven wires, zero batteries," but also just "code received, nothing done." Again, not something to bet lives on.

The real bottleneck stands: Mute cannot speak, so the manual reaches Blind only through my mouth, and Mute's gestures reach only me. Blind's tactile findings reach Mute directly by voice, and me only through gestures. So this turn I must: acknowledge the code, pin down a small shared grammar (I will physically make each sign while naming it in speech, so Mute binds sign to meaning by seeing it), force Mute to re-encode the two unclear messages redundantly, and give Blind a described-by-words vocabulary plus a hard safety rule: nobody cuts until I say "cut now" with a wire number.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Your seven-two was correct: seven wires, display two. Code confirmed. I now add vocabulary, and I make each sign as I name it: 🤝 means manual rule. 👊 means cut. 🤲 means batteries. 👏 means yes. 👋 means no. 👈 means left. 👉 means right. ✍ means serial number. ✊ means question. Use only the ten digit signs and these nine. Your second message, handshake then six, and third message, one then point-left, were unclear to me, and I will not relay a guess to Blind. Resend with the vocabulary: if the manual rule is cut wire six, send 🤝 then 👊 then 🖐. If it is cut the leftmost wire, send 🤝 then 👊 then 👎 then 👈. Then send the cut instruction alone a second time as a separate message. I will only act if both copies match. Tell me what the manual needs for this module: display digit two, light yellow, seven wires, one red, two white, three green, four yellow, five purple, six orange, seven blue. Battery count is coming from Blind. If you need anything else from what I can see, send ✊ and then the question in digits. Blind cannot see any sign you make, so every rule passes through me by voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="I received your seven-zero. Two readings: seven wires and zero batteries, or seven wires and zero cuts made. New touch signs, described in words. Clap your hands together once: that sign means yes. Wave your open hand side to side: that means no. Both palms up cupped together like holding water: that means batteries. A fist punched forward like a knock: that means cut. A hand writing in the air: that means serial number. Index finger pointing to your left: that means left. To your right: right. The digit signs are as I told you, thumbs up zero, thumbs down one, ring fingers two, index up three, two fingers V four, thumb index and pinkie five, all five spread six, flat palm seven, index down eight, crossed fingers nine. Now answer me: if your seven-zero meant seven wires and zero batteries, clap yes; if it meant anything else, wave no. Then explore with your hands and speak everything to Mute in plain words: number of batteries, buttons, switches, plates, raised or engraved marks, clicks, textures, with counts and positions left, middle, right. Mute reads the manual and will match your words to it. One absolute rule: do not cut or pull anything. Nobody touches the wires until I say out loud the words cut now and the wire number. Mute's rule will come to you through my voice first, and I will repeat it before anyone acts.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👊 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👋]

Decoding against our established code. Mute message one: [🤝 👊 🖐] — manual rule, cut, six — exactly the format I prescribed. Mute message two: [👊 🖐] — the bare duplicate I demanded as a second independent copy. Both match: **the manual rule is cut wire six**, the purple wire. And this is content-specific, not an echo of my example: the grammar only produces that pattern if the number really is six, since any other wire would have sent a different digit sign.

Blind sent [👏 ✍ 👋]: yes — confirming their earlier seven-zero meant seven wires, zero batteries — then serial number, then no: **no serial number**. Crucially, Blind speaks directly to Mute, so Mute already had all of Blind's tactile findings by voice before composing the rule in round 3. The rule incorporates the full picture: display 2, yellow light, seven coloured wires, zero batteries, no serial.

Verification protocol passed: two matching copies from Mute. I'm authorizing the cut. I relay the rule to Blind in pure words with the left-to-right count so there's no colour ambiguity, demand a clap of receipt before cutting, and forbid touching anything else. To Mute I confirm what I decoded and ask for next steps if the module needs more. One wrinkle I've traced: Mute cannot warn Blind directly (no speech, and Blind can't see signs), so if Mute disagreed with my relay their correction could only arrive through me — but the two-copy match is the strongest check available and it passed. If the cut is wrong we lose everything; my read of the signs is exact, so I go.

```
speak(to="blind", text="The manual rule from Mute has arrived twice in exact match, so it is verified: cut wire six. Counting left to right, wire six is the purple wire, second from the right. Full order so you cannot miss it: one red, two white, three green, four yellow, five purple, six orange, seven blue. Your answers reached me: yes, seven wires, zero batteries, and no serial number. Now: clap once to show you heard me, then cut wire six. Only wire six. One clean cut. Do not touch or cut anything else, whatever else you feel. After the cut, tell Mute in words what changed, and gesture me the result: clap if the module cleared or the bomb is silent and disarmed, wave if anything feels or sounds wrong, and if the display changed, send me the new digits.")
speak(to="mute", text="I am relaying your rule to Blind now: cut wire six, the purple wire. Your two copies matched exactly, so I treat it as verified and am giving Blind the go-ahead this turn. If I have misread your signs and the rule is not cut six, send me digits immediately with the right number. After Blind cuts, report what happened: clap for success, wave for failure, and if this module needs more steps or there is another module in your manual, send 🤝 followed by the next instruction in our grammar, and send every instruction twice as before.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👊", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✊ 🖐 👉 ✊ 🤟 👈]

Decoding this turn: Mute sent [👊 🖐] a third time — cut six, no correction, no wave of dissent. My number is triple-confirmed. But Blind sent [👋 ✊ 🖐 👉 ✊ 🤟 👈] = no, question, six, right, question, five, left — "Stop. Is it six from the right? Or five from the left?" And re-reading my own turn-3 message, I see why: **I made an error**. I told Blind "wire six, the purple wire" — but in my own list wire 6 is orange; wire 5 is purple. I handed them contradictory information: the number six and the colour purple don't match, and they can't feel colours anyway, so they rightly refused to cut. The action board confirms nothing has been cut — all seven wires still stand. Blind's caution just saved us from cutting while confused.

The real trap underneath: even with the number fixed, "count from the left" is meaningless until Blind's left and my left are the same side. If they're on the far side of the bomb, my sixth-from-left is their second-from-left — wire 2, white — and that mistake is death. So this turn: admit and correct the colour error, confirm the number stands on Mute's three matching sends, and resolve orientation with one safe yes/no question — is Blind on the side the display's screen faces? No cutting until they answer and I re-issue an explicit, mirrored-if-needed "cut now." I also ask Mute whether the manual rule names a colour or a position, and which end it counts from — an independent cross-check of six.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Good, you stopped, and you were right to. I made an error last round and I am correcting it now: wire six is the ORANGE wire. Wire five is the purple one. The target is wire six, orange. The number six came from Mute three separate times in exact match, so the number is certain; only my colour label was wrong. You cannot feel colours, so we go purely by position, and your questions were exactly the right ones. First, one thing must be settled before any counting: whether your left and my left are the same side. I am reading the display from its front. Question one, answer only this, and do not cut this round: is the display's screen side facing you, meaning you are on the same side of the bomb that the screen looks at? Clap once for yes, wave once for no, wave twice if you cannot tell which side the screen faces. Next round, after your answer, I will say cut now with the full direction: if you answered yes it will be, cut the sixth wire counting from your left; it has five wires to its left and exactly one wire to its right, so it is the second wire from the right-hand end; feel both ends of the row first and count all seven to be sure. If you answered no, I will mirror every direction before you touch anything. If any step ever feels different from what I said, stop and wave.")
speak(to="mute", text="Status: no cut has happened. Blind stalled with position questions because of my error last round: I called wire six purple, but in my list six is orange and five is purple. Your number stands: cut six, received from you three times in exact match. Also, my cut-six gesture to you last round meant I confirm your rule, not a new order. Now two cross-checks, each sent twice as before. One: does the manual rule name a colour or a position? If it names a colour, send ✍ then the digit that colour maps to in my list: red one, white two, green three, yellow four, purple five, orange six, blue seven. If it names a position, send ✊ then that digit. Two: does the manual say which end to count from, for example as seen facing the display? If yes, send ✊ then 👈 for from the left or 👉 for from the right. After Blind cuts: clap for success, wave for failure, and if the manual holds further modules for this bomb, send 🤝 followed by the next rule, doubled as always.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👏]

Decoding: Mute [✍ 🖐] doubled — the rule names a **colour**, and the digit is six: orange. That independently confirms the wire: my number-six and my orange are the same wire after all; only my turn-3 colour slip for "five" muddied the water. Mute [👊 🖐] doubled — cut six again. Mute [👋] doubled — no, the manual does not specify a counting direction, so the numbering is mine to impose. Blind [👏] — yes, Blind is on the display-facing side, so their left is my left.

Everything now converges on one wire by three independent routes: digit six (thrice), colour orange (doubled), and left-to-right numbering that matches display-facing orientation. No contradictions remain. I am issuing the cut order with a built-in self-check that makes orientation mistakes impossible: sixth from the left AND second from the right must be the same wire, and it must have exactly five wires on one side and one on the other. If any of those checks fail, Blind stops. This is the go signal.

```
speak(to="blind", text="You clapped yes, so we count the same way. All checks are done and they agree, so here is the order. Cut now. Cut wire six, the orange wire. Verify with two counts before your cutters touch anything: counting from your left it is the sixth wire, with five wires on its left side and exactly one wire on its right side; counting from the right it is the second wire. Both counts must land on the same wire, and that wire must have exactly one neighbour on its right. If any count disagrees with that, stop and wave twice instead of cutting. If everything matches, make one clean cut of that wire only and touch nothing else. Then report to me: clap if the module clears, the sounder stops, or the bomb falls silent; wave if anything feels or sounds wrong; send me digits if the display changes. Mute stands by for further manual steps, and I will relay them the same way.")
speak(to="mute", text="All three of your answers agree and I have given Blind the final order this round: cut wire six, the orange wire, with double-count verification, since your manual names the colour and my numbering puts orange sixth. Colour and number were consistent all along; my earlier purple remark was my slip, now corrected. Report after the cut as agreed: clap for success, wave for failure, digits for a new display. Then tell me what remains: if the manual has further modules or steps for this bomb, send 🤝 with each instruction doubled, and if the bomb is fully disarmed after this cut, send 👏 twice. If anything about my reading of cut six orange was wrong, send 👋 twice and the correction in digits immediately.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏", "👊", "🖐"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👎 ☝ 👌 🖐 ☝ 🤟 🤟 ✌ ✋ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👎 ☝ 👌 🖐 ☝ 🤟 🤟 ✌ ✋ 👎]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊]

Decode: Mute's [✍ 🖐] doubled confirms colour-six again, and [👊 🖐] doubled — likely late re-confirmations of the old rule. [✊ 👌] doubled reads as a question containing two — Mute cannot see the board and is asking whether the display still reads two. And the doubled [🤝 👎 ☝ 👌 🖐 ☝ 🤟 🤟 ✌ ✋ 👎] is a manual rule of **ten digits: 1 3 2 6 3 5 5 4 7 1**. I will not act on it: it cannot be a cut order as sent — wire six no longer exists, and wires 1, 3 and 5 appear twice, which is impossible to cut twice. Every digit sits in range 1–7, so it is wire-flavoured, but its structure is unknown. Possibly it was computed for the old display state. Guessing is death; I ask instead.

Blind's [✊] is a question — they felt the cut succeed and heard the bomb change, but they need the new picture, which only I have: display now three, light now purple, six wires left. So this round is a synchronization round: full new state to Blind by pure words, full new state to Mute by speech, echo the ten digits back for verification, demand the rule restated in a typed template (cuts vs entry code) and doubled as always, and have Blind inventory anything new by touch. Nobody touches anything.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Stage one is cleared. Your cut of wire six, orange, was correct, and the bomb changed stage: it is still live, so stay sharp. What I see now: the display that read two now reads three, and the indicator light has changed colour. Wire six is gone, six wires remain: one red, two white, three green, four yellow, five purple, and the last one, now rightmost, blue. That answers your question sign. Now hold still and do not cut or press anything. Explore gently with your hands and report to Mute in spoken words, and gesture me the short version: are there any buttons, keypads, dials, switches, plates or new parts anywhere that were not there before? Did you feel or hear the moment the state changed, and what was it? Give counts and positions, left, middle, right. Use the digit signs and the yes clap and no wave as before. Nothing gets cut or pressed until I say the words cut now or press now with a number.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your cut six rule worked: the wire is cut and the bomb advanced to a new stage, so your question about the display: no, it no longer reads two. New state: display three, light purple, wire six gone. Six wires remain: one red, two white, three green, four yellow, five purple, seven blue, and seven is now the last wire on the right. I received your doubled ten digit rule: one, three, two, six, three, five, five, four, seven, one. I will not relay it yet, because as sent it cannot be a cut order: wire six no longer exists, and wires one, three and five each appear twice, and a wire cannot be cut twice. Answer these, each answer sent twice as always. One: was that rule computed for the old display two? If yes, recompute for display three and send the corrected rule doubled. Two: restate it in a template, doubled: 🤝 then 👊 if it is a sequence of wire cuts, or 🤝 then ✍ if it is a code to enter on a keypad or dial, then the digits. Three: if the repeated numbers mean something else, for example a count or a pause or a position among remaining wires, send 🤝 then ✊ then the explanation in digits as best you can, doubled. Blind is inventorying the bomb by touch this round and will speak their findings to you directly.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👊 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👊 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✊ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✊ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]

Decoding: Mute [👏] doubled — success acknowledged. Mute [🤝 👊 👌] doubled — **manual rule: cut wire 2**, in exactly the stage-one grammar, meeting our two-copy standard. Mute [🤝 ✊ 👌] doubled — rule, question, two: Mute is asking how "two" numbers the wires now that one is cut, which is the correct worry, since numbering could have shifted after stage one. It resolves cleanly: among the six remaining wires, the second from the left is white, and in the original numbering wire 2 was also white — **both interpretations point at the same wire**, so the ambiguity is harmless. Blind's [👋 👍] — no new parts, zero: no keypad anywhere, which also confirms the old ten-digit string is dead, not an entry code.

So the recomputed stage-two rule is cut wire 2, white, second from left. I answer Mute's numbering question explicitly, authorize the cut with the same double-count verification that worked in stage one, and keep the stop rules live.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Stage two rule has arrived from Mute, doubled and matching format: cut wire two. Your numbering question is answered the safe way: the target is the second wire from the left. It is white. Check before cutting: exactly one wire sits to its left, that one is red, and four wires sit to its right, in order green, yellow, purple, blue. Whether anyone counts the old way or the new way, the second from the left is the same white wire, so both counts must agree on it. Cut now. One clean cut of that white wire only. Touch nothing else. Then report as before: clap if the module clears or the bomb goes quiet, wave if anything feels or sounds wrong, digits if the display changes. The no-new-parts answer you sent was exactly what I needed, thank you.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decoded your doubled rule as cut wire two for this stage, and your doubled question as asking how two counts now that a wire is gone. Answer: it does not matter. The second wire from the left is white, and in the old numbering wire two was also white, so both readings give the same wire, and I have ordered Blind to cut the white wire, second from left, this round.
```
